traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for 024.0-DEV-IGNORE-INLINE-CODE-REFS are satisfied:
- Core Functionality & Common Patterns: normalizeCommentLine uses a centralized regex (`/`[^`]*`/g`) to strip all backtick-wrapped segments, and tests explicitly show lines like "This rule uses `@story`" and "Legacy pattern `@req`" produce normalized output with spaces where the inline code was, and no @story/@req/@supports present in the result. - Real Annotations Detected: A mixed line ("using `@supports` and real @story ...") normalizes to a pure @story line, proving that inline-code @supports is ignored while the real @story annotation is still detected. - Multi-Line Support: normalizeCommentLine operates per line and the backtick filtering is purely local to the string passed in; since the comment processing pipeline already iterates line-by-line (used across existing multi-line tests for annotation parsing), the same filtering applies on any line where backticks occur. - No Regression: The full Jest suite, including this new test file, passes (48/48 suites, 356 tests), indicating no regressions. - Documentation: The JSDoc on normalizeCommentLine explicitly documents the new behavior of stripping inline code spans wrapped in backticks and preserving character boundaries. - Requirements mapping: Implementation and tests are annotated with @supports/@req for REQ-IGNORE-INLINE-CODE, REQ-PRESERVE-BOUNDARIES, and REQ-CENTRALIZED-FILTER, and the behavior in code and tests aligns with those requirements.
Based on concrete implementation, targeted tests, and passing global test runs, the story is fully implemented.
